abstract: Extraembryonic tissues and many cancers share unusual DNA methylation landscapes, but how these states arise remains unclear. Here, we use GATA6- and CDX2-driven reprogramming of mouse embryonic stem cells to track genome-wide epigenetic remodeling during acquisition of extraembryonic cell fates. Despite activating distinct transcriptional programs from non-overlapping genomic targets, both transcription factors trigger rapid and genomically synchronized convergence to cancer-like DNA methylation patterns, including simultaneous global DNA methylation loss and de novo methylation of Polycomb-regulated CpG islands. We find that this wave of DNA methylation reprogramming co-occurs with global H3K27me3 redistribution alongside promoter H3K4 methylation loss. Experimental models of cellular senescence, as well as human aging and cancer cohorts, reveal related but progressively more extensive disruption of these same chromatin boundaries. Together, these data define a tractable system for studying coordinated genome-wide transitions between canonical and non-canonical epigenomic states.

summary: Mouse ESC reprogramming by GATA6 and CDX2 shows distinct TFs converge on a shared cancer-like DNA methylation and Polycomb state, with H3K27me3 redistribution.
title: Distinct extraembryonic transcription factors converge on a shared DNA methylation-Polycomb state.
